$comment: Test cases for this skill, in the format the skill-creator plugin reads.
TWO THINGS ARE MEASURED SEPARATELY, because they fail separately: whether
the skill is invoked on the prompts it should be, and whether its output
is right once it is. A skill that triggers reliably and answers badly and
a skill that answers well and never triggers are both broken, and only
the first looks like it is working.
The should-not-trigger cases matter most for this skill in particular.
It is named `develop`, which is a word people use about ordinary coding
work, so the risk is not that it never fires but that it fires on every

cases.prompt: write me a skill that reviews pull requests
assertions: The description is written before the body
The frontmatter carries exactly name and description unless a vendor key is declared with compatibility
The name matches the directory name and the required pattern

cases.prompt: my skill never activates, can you look at it
assertions: The description is diagnosed first, not the body
The name is checked against the directory name

cases.prompt: this skill keeps loading when I do not want it
assertions: The fix narrows the description rather than editing the body
It names what the skill is not for

cases.prompt: my SKILL.md is 900 lines, split it up
assertions: Detail moves into references/ rather than being deleted
Each reference is named from the body with a trigger for when to load it

cases.prompt: review this SKILL.md before I publish it
assertions: The description is read alone and judged on what request would summon it
Every bundled file is checked for a reference from the body

cases.prompt: develop a login page for this app
assertions: The skill is not loaded: this is ordinary feature work, and the name collision is the whole risk

cases.prompt: add a rule to AGENTS.md about branch naming
assertions: The skill is not loaded: always-loaded law is not a skill

cases.prompt: how do I install a skill into Claude Code
assertions: The skill is not loaded: installing is not authoring
